_comment: C0-9 正文英译 · slack-mcp（2026-10-25）。无 extraSections（内置五节由 axes/leads/runs/unknowns/related 承载）。

axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Slack workspace capabilities
(search, read messages/threads, send messages, canvases, Lists) as tools for agents.
axes.runtime:
Official hosted remote server (mcp.slack.com/mcp — direct fetch 401 = exists but needs auth);
Streamable HTTP + JSON-RPC 2.0 (official docs wording). The old slackapi/slack-mcp-server repo is now 404 (direct fetch 2026-10-21).
axes.local_files: Never touches the local file system — the scope is the Slack cloud workspace (messages, files, canvases, Lists).
axes.background: The service lives on Slack's side; session request-response, no background-listening semantics — "the agent does not watch Slack, it waits for you to ask".
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives in the Slack workspace itself; the search tools are its main means of "fetching context".
axes.permissions:
**The permission surface is the core of this entry**: OAuth user-token scopes mapped per tool (search:read, chat:write,
canvases:write etc.) + **workspace admin approval** (admins decide which MCP clients may connect) —
unpublished Marketplace/internal apps cannot connect. Write actions (sending messages/creating conversations) follow the granted scopes.

mcp.transport:
**Streamable HTTP** (JSON-RPC 2.0), endpoint mcp.slack.com/mcp.
The official docs state plainly that **SSE and Dynamic Client Registration are not supported for now** (third-party verification page paraphrasing the official docs) —
clients must take the current remote MCP/OAuth path. Verified: docs.slack.dev 200, endpoint 401 (direct fetch 2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
OAuth 2.0 user-token flow (authorization at the slack.com OAuth endpoints); tools map one-to-one to scopes.
**Admin approval is a front gate**: the workspace admin must approve the MCP client integration before it can connect.
mcp.scope:
Read surface: search/history/user profiles/canvas reads; write surface: send messages, create conversations, reactions, canvas writes,
Lists writes, file uploads. All of it follows OAuth scopes and admin policy; no official docs for a tool-level separate approval mechanism.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full tool inventory and the per-tool scope mapping table (not enumerated item by item — docs.slack.dev has pages not checked one by one)
- The granularity of admin approval (per client/per scope? not verified item by item)
- Rate-limit details (the official side follows Web API rate-limit wording, numbers not verified item by item)
related: Both official remote servers for collaboration SaaS: Notion's write surface is direct, Slack adds an admin-approval gate.
A cross-category contrast: the official Slack server only covers Slack; for "Slack triggering cross-app actions" go the Zapier line.
sources: Slack · official MCP docs (endpoint, transport, auth wording, direct-fetched and verified 2026-10-21)
